page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors running at 3.9 GHz, configured with 32 physical cores and 64 virtual central processing units (vCPUs) via two threads per core. System memory totals 512.0 GB, providing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, designed for workloads that require substantial memory capacity relative to compute resources.

For local storage, the instance includes 3800 GB of bundled NVMe SSD instance store capacity, facilitating high-throughput, low-latency I/O directly attached to the host. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 67 Gbps managed via the Nitro architecture. The configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators and does not offer complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The combination of high-density memory, dedicated multi-core Intel processing, integrated high-speed NVMe storage, and 67 Gbps networking presents strong architectural efficiency for data-heavy workloads without requiring external block storage for high-frequency operations. However, the temporary nature of instance store volumes necessitates separate strategies for persistent state. Typical deployment targets include in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, distributed analytics engines, and transactional database workloads requiring substantial scratch space.

This configuration fits high-throughput transactional databases, large in-memory caches, distributed real-time analytics engines, and heavy ETL data pipelines.
